## Claims
- [source-backed] The paper formally conjectures that both Schur-function generating sets
  \[
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\},
  \]
  for \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), are minimal; each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1380-1421; source-2, lines 1489-1502]
- [source-backed] The stronger unresolved statement is
  \[
  J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}},
  \]
  and the authors explicitly state that a proof had eluded them. [source-2, lines 1536-1552]
- [proved] Let \(M\) be a bounded-below graded module over a connected graded ring \(\Lambda\), and let \(G\) be either homogeneous family above. If the image of \(G\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(M/\Lambda_+M\), then \(G\) is a minimal \(\Lambda\)-generating family. Indeed, the source’s graded Nakayama proposition identifies generation and inclusion-minimality with spanning and minimal spanning in \(M/\Lambda_+M\); a basis is minimally spanning. [source-2, lines 1520-1534]
- [proved] A rational rank calculation cannot prove the stronger statement or minimality integrally: \(2\in\mathbb Z\) is a basis after tensoring with \(\mathbb Q\), but does not generate \(\mathbb Z\); and \(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\) has a minimal one-element generating set but is not free. Thus a direct proof must exclude both nonunit indices and torsion.
- [unsupported] The directory reports a separate open question: determine minimal generating sets for general type-\(A\) ideals \(I_w\); the cited primary-source passage is not supplied here, so this identification is not independently primary-source verified. [source-6, lines 88-102]

## Strategy
For either proposed family \(G\), compute the integral graded quotient
\[
Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v
\]
in a Schur basis. A sufficient direct certificate is an integral presentation whose relation matrix has Smith diagonal \((1,\ldots,1,0,\ldots,0)\), with the surviving proposed classes forming the free coordinates. This proves \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) and then minimality by the preceding criterion.

## Gaps
No all-degree integral presentation of \(Q\), Smith-form calculation, or torsion-exclusion proof is supplied here. Existing bounded Pieri calculations cannot by themselves control relations in all degrees. Independent review is not present in the supplied material.

## Next
A viable bounded follow-up is to prove an all-degree Schur-basis presentation for one new parameter family and exhibit unimodular elimination retaining one of the two proposed generator families.
